newsitem.title: FRANCE: EP demands more money for research.
newsitem.headline: EP demands more money for research.

text.p: The European Parliament criticised EU governments on Thursday for refusing to accept a substantial increase in European Union funding for research and technological development (RTD) over the next two years.
The parliament supports a European Commission recommendation -- COM(96)453 -- for a 700-million-ecu increase in the budget of the EU's fourth RTD framework programme (1994-1998).
But EU ministers said they were only prepared to allocate an extra 100 million ecus, to prevent the EU's overall budget surpassing its fixed ceiling.
Parliament, which has joint powers with the Council of Ministers over the research budget, insisted in a report adopted on Thursday that a 200-million-ecu increase was the minimum acceptable.

Euro-MPs said the increases should be allocated to a new research programme on renewable energy (33 million ecus) and to doubling the funds for existing programmes on telematics, information technology, industrial and materials technology, the environment and climate change.
Parliament requested a further 20 million ecus for research into the detection and destruction of landmines.

Parliament's report, drafted by German Socialist Rolf Linkhor, noted that of the 100 million ecus it was prepared to add to the research budget, the Council had earmarked 35 million -- over a third -- for research into mad cow disease (BSE), vaccines and viral infections.

Parliament conceded research into bovine spongiform encephalopathy was essential because of the health hazards but protested that the money should have been found elsewhere, rather than draining resources from other priority research areas.
If, as seems likely, the Council refuses to accept Parliament's amendments to the text, the two sides will have to launch conciliation talks.
